stories.headline: One Nation wins first lower house seat at Farrer by-election, triggering Liberal Party crisis
stories.summary: One Nation candidate David Farley won the Farrer by-election on May 10, giving the party its first-ever seat in the federal House of Representatives and stripping a seat the Liberal-National Coalition had held for 77 years. The result prompted intense debate about the Coalition's future, with Opposition Leader Angus Taylor acknowledging an 'existential situation' and Prime Minister Albanese accusing the Liberals of legitimising One Nation by directing preferences to them.

stories.headline: RBA raises cash rate third consecutive time to 4.35%, signals pause as inflation forecasts revised upward
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised the cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.35% on May 5 in an 8-1 vote, its third consecutive hike in 2026, citing persistent inflation exacerbated by the US-Iran conflict's impact on fuel prices. Governor Michele Bullock signalled a pause to assess conditions, though the RBA's updated forecasts implied a terminal rate near 4.7% by year-end, prompting banks to revise further hike expectations to August and September.

stories.headline: IS-linked women return from Syria, three charged with slavery and terrorism offences
stories.summary: A group of four women and nine children who had spent years at Roj camp in Syria arrived in Australia on two Qatar Airways flights on May 7–8. Three of the women were arrested at Melbourne and Sydney airports and charged with slavery and terrorism offences including crimes against humanity; a fourth was also charged. Prime Minister Albanese declared 'zero sympathy' for the adults while expressing support for the children, and ASIO chief Mike Burgess stated the return did not change the national terrorism threat level.

stories.headline: Australia-Fiji Vuvale Union treaty finalised; China blocks parallel Vanuatu deal
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Penny Wong and Pacific Minister Pat Conroy travelled to Fiji May 6–8 and finalised the Vuvale Union, a treaty-level security and economic agreement, while Fiji's cabinet formally approved it. Australia also committed A$30 million to help Fiji manage fuel price shocks. Separately, reports emerged that China had intervened to undermine a similar A$500 million treaty between Australia and Vanuatu, highlighting Canberra's competition with Beijing for Pacific influence.

stories.headline: Albanese government's May 12 federal budget to include negative gearing and CGT overhaul, reversing pre-election pledge
stories.summary: The Albanese government confirmed its May 12 budget will include changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax concessions, reversing promises made before the 2025 election. Reports revealed a secret cabinet subcommittee had been planning the changes for months. The budget will also address housing affordability, provide business tax relief, and include housing policy measures, amid debate about broken promises and the government's mandate to act beyond its election platform.

stories.headline: Australia-Japan summit: Albanese and Takaichi sign economic security declaration covering energy, defence, critical minerals
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi visited Australia on May 4–6, signing a joint declaration on Economic Security Cooperation with Prime Minister Albanese covering energy security, critical minerals (including a A$1.3bn project), and defence, as both countries navigate supply chain disruptions from the Iran conflict. Foreign Minister Wong dismissed suggestions that Japan could serve as a backup for Australia's AUKUS submarine deal.

stories.headline: Albanese announces $10.7 billion fuel security package including government-owned reserve and east coast gas reservation
stories.summary: Prime Minister Albanese unveiled a $10.7 billion fuel security package on May 6, including $3.2 billion for a government-owned onshore fuel reserve and $7.5 billion in loans, equity and guarantees, framed as a response to global supply disruptions from the US-Iran conflict. Separately, energy companies were announced to be required to reserve gas for the domestic east coast market from July next year. Deputy PM Marles confirmed no US request for Australian naval support in the Strait of Hormuz had been received, though conversations were ongoing.

stories.headline: Liberal Party leadership turmoil: Tony Abbott seeks party presidency amid post-Farrer crisis
stories.summary: Former Prime Minister Tony Abbott emerged as a candidate for the Liberal Party's federal presidency in the aftermath of the Farrer by-election loss, with leader Angus Taylor weighing whether to publicly back him. Moderate Liberals feared Abbott's platform would overshadow Taylor's leadership, while Abbott's supporters argued his internal reform credentials were needed to rebuild the party.

stories.headline: Inland Rail Melbourne-Brisbane link abandoned as cost blows out beyond $45 billion
stories.summary: The Albanese government announced it would drastically scale back the Inland Rail project, abandoning plans to connect country New South Wales and Queensland by rail and limiting the project to a shorter Beveridge (Victoria) to Parkes (NSW) corridor, as the project's cost estimate exceeded $45 billion.

stories.headline: Budget funds new ASIO-led counter-terrorism online centre; scrutiny of ASIO funding priorities intensifies
stories.summary: The budget allocated $74 million over two years for a new Counter-Terrorism Online Centre to be jointly led by ASIO and the Australian Federal Police, targeting high-risk online spaces including social media and gaming platforms. Separately, an analysis of ASIO's annual reports alleged that counter-espionage had absorbed a greater share of resources at the expense of counter-terrorism, raising questions about whether the agency was adequately funded ahead of the Bondi terror attack royal commission hearings.

stories.headline: Five Eyes agencies (including Australia) publish joint guidance warning against rapid agentic AI deployment

The guidance urged prioritising resilience over productivity.

stories.summary: Leaders of Pacific Islands Forum countries, including Australia, formally invoked the Biketawa Declaration to prompt a coordinated regional response to the global fuel crisis stemming from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the forum's highest-level crisis response mechanism.

stories.headline: Hantavirus outbreak on cruise ship: Australia charters flight to repatriate nationals
stories.summary: Australia's government chartered a flight through Perth to repatriate four Australian citizens and one permanent resident from the MV Hondius, a luxury cruise ship struck by a hantavirus outbreak. Federal environment minister Murray Watt confirmed quarantine arrangements were being finalised with state governments.

stories.summary: An Australian activist who attempted to break Israel's naval blockade of Gaza as part of a flotilla returned home after being detained by Israeli authorities, while two other non-Australian participants remained in Israeli custody. Critics accused PM Albanese and Foreign Minister Wong of being missing in action in securing consular support for the detained Australians.

stories.headline: Australia's antisemitism royal commission hears personal testimonies on growing hostility
stories.summary: An antisemitism royal commission held hearings in which Jewish Australians provided personal testimonies about increased hostility, discrimination, and the impact of the Bondi terror attack, with debate around the difficulty of separating criticism of Israel's government from antisemitism.

stories.headline: Australia's petro-diplomacy: Wong visits China to push resumption of fuel exports
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Penny Wong flew to China to press for the resumption of jet fuel sales to Australian businesses, leveraging Australia's status as a major LNG and coal exporter to encourage Beijing to relax export curbs imposed after the US-Iran conflict disrupted global supply chains.

articles.title: Australia's 'petro-diplomacy' eases fuel shortage fears

stories.headline: New Zealand opens frigate replacement discussions with Australia and Britain
stories.summary: New Zealand's Defence Minister Chris Penk confirmed discussions with Australia and Britain had begun over replacing New Zealand's ageing Anzac-class frigates, with two options under consideration including the Japanese Mogami-class (chosen by Australia) and Britain's Type 31. A preferred path is expected to go to government by end of 2027.
